title: An AI Future Without the Lock-In — Remy Guercio, Tailscale
talk_summary: A Tailscale engineer pitches their AI gateway (Aperture) as a way to avoid vendor lock-in by decoupling four layers of an internal AI deployment: LLMs, data connectors/MCP, interfaces, and sandboxes. The core actionable idea is centralizing model/MCP access behind an identity-aware gateway so you can swap providers, enforce per-identity budgets, and inspect agent logs.

takeaways.technique: Identity-aware gateway with per-identity model budgets
takeaways.what_they_do: A gateway sits between agents and all LLM/MCP endpoints; it identifies the caller (user or tagged machine like a PR review bot) and grants model access plus budgets by identity, e.g. unlimited on a cheap model but a narrow budget on a frontier model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you get unlimited budget with a cheap model and you get an extremely narrow budget with a Frontier model

takeaways.technique: Centralized usage logging to diagnose wasted tokens
takeaways.what_they_do: Because all traffic passes through the gateway, they can see sessions that run hundreds/thousands of messages without clearing context and diagnose runaway agent loops after the fact.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the number of sessions that are hundreds or thousands of messages long where nobody clears the context
takeaways.numbers: sessions of tens of millions of tokens with cache maxed out

takeaways.technique: Post-hoc log analysis by pointing an agent at its own traces
takeaways.what_they_do: When an agent spirals without reaching an answer, they point a model back at the gateway logs to ask what went wrong, since cheap models are bad at stopping but good at analyzing failures afterward.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they are great at analyzing where they went wrong after the fact

takeaways.technique: Single authenticated MCP/API endpoint per identity
takeaways.what_they_do: MCP servers and APIs are configured once at the gateway; agents authenticate by network identity so switching tools/frameworks requires no re-auth, lowering friction to experiment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all they have to do is hit that endpoint and if they're on the tail net everything's authenticated as them

takeaways.what_they_do: They plan to add a sandbox orchestration layer to the gateway so all environments (LLMs, data, sandboxes) are visible and swappable from one place.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We're actually going to be adding kind of an orchestration layer as well for sandboxes to a gateway
